claims.statement: EU WEEE rules require item-level functionality evidence, transfer documentation, a non-waste declaration, and protective packaging to substantiate cross-border shipment as used EEE rather than WEEE; absent the required proof, authorities may treat the load as WEEE and presume an illegal shipment.

Polish WEEE law requires compliant storage and transport, directs collectors to authorized processing plants, and reserves dismantling and preparation for reuse of equipment already classified as WEEE to processing plants.

For waste industrial, EV, and light-means-of-transport batteries prepared for reuse or repurposing, EU battery rules require state-of-health evidence and documentation of further use through an invoice or ownership-transfer contract before demonstrating that the battery is no longer waste.
The EU General Product Safety Regulation applies to used, repaired, and reconditioned consumer products made available on the market, so resale does not eliminate product-safety duties.

Established operators already cover much of the proposed downstream stack: PV CYCLE provides EU-wide compliance, collection, preparation-for-reuse, and treatment services, while SecondSol markets new, used, and refurbished renewable equipment and offers buyback, testing, repair, logistics, and recycling.

PV CYCLE reports rising PV-system waste and reuse activity but also says second-hand PV lacks mature international guidance, which supports both a growing supply event and material grading/safety uncertainty.

contrary_evidence: If an item is already WEEE in Poland, preparation for reuse and dismantling cannot lawfully be performed as an informal outsourced test or parts-harvesting step outside an authorized processing plant.
PV CYCLE already offers EU-wide collection and treatment, and SecondSol already combines a large professional secondary marketplace with buyback, testing, repair, fulfillment, and recycling.
PV CYCLE characterizes waste treatment as high-volume and low-return and reports that second-hand PV still lacks mature international guidance, weakening assumptions of easy grading and wide margins.
Used or refurbished products sold to consumers remain subject to product-safety obligations.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: embed one pre-removal disposition checkpoint in planned commercial PV string-inverter replacement work orders at the family installer in one dense Wielkopolska service area; expansion to other installers occurs only if the paid workflow repeats. The family connection is evidence of pilot access, not of a signed agreement, paid adoption, exclusivity, or transferable acquisition economics.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unproven hypothesis: equity value could emerge only if a paid pre-removal workflow repeats across installer clusters and its serial-level routing data improves decisions or partner terms without proportional founder labor. No adoption, contribution margin, retention, scalable acquisition, or valuation evidence currently supports the founder wealth objective.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: one equipment class, one region, standardized intake, and direct partner handoffs could fit part-time operation; actual exception volume, legal review, partner coordination, disputes, and hours per work order must be measured before claiming founder compatibility.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Evidence: regulated physical work must remain with appropriate partners, downstream incumbents exist, and no fee, quote, or margin has been validated. Hypothesis: the fixed service fee must cover intake, route documentation, partner coordination, legal and insurance allocation, and exceptions without any resale proceeds; brokerage is zero in the conservative case. Margin remains unknown until paid work orders and full activity-based costs are observed.
economics.payback: Unknown. Measure acquisition effort, paid-work-order conversion, time per order, legal and insurance allocation, partner coordination cost, refunds or disputes, and repeat work; do not count a contingent buyer bid or brokerage fee until a compliant transfer actually closes.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: quote a fixed per-work-order fee before removal for the documented route decision, with an optional disclosed brokerage fee only after a professional transfer closes. No amount, acceptance rate, buyer price, or willingness to pay is assumed; the pilot must test whether the fixed fee covers fully loaded service cost independently of salvage.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: an installer with recurring replacement work may reuse a low-friction embedded checkpoint if it reduces documented handling effort or risk. No repeat rate is evidenced; measure repeat paid work orders separately from one-off family-installer access.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: If the paid workflow is adopted, serial-level partner quotes, route decisions, realized costs, transfer outcomes, returns, and buyer requirements could improve bid gates and partner selection; no exclusive supply right, proprietary dataset, or compounding advantage exists yet
fingerprint.customer: Initial pilot hypothesis: regional PV installers performing planned commercial string-inverter replacements in one dense Wielkopolska service area; equipment owners, professional buyers, and authorized operators are workflow counterparties rather than assumed paying customers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Propose the pre-removal checkpoint inside the family installer's planned commercial string-inverter replacement work orders in one dense region, then approach other installers only with measured paid-work-order economics; no signed workflow mandate, exclusivity, or transferable channel is assumed
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A one-equipment-class, no-custody pre-removal disposition gate: collect title, serial, condition, and job data before removal; request a contingent professional-buyer bid and an authorized-operator route quote; coordinate a direct owner-to-buyer transfer only when the evidence supports product status and the bid covers every enumerated landed cost, otherwise route directly to the authorized operator. The venture does not acquire inventory or perform transport, storage, testing, dismantling, or waste handling; revenue is hypothesized as a pre-quoted workflow fee plus a contingent brokerage fee only after a completed professional transfer
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Unvalidated hypothesis: the installer pays a pre-quoted service fee when the venture completes the pre-removal evidence pack and issues a documented direct-transfer or authorized-operator route; a professional buyer pays the owner under a contingent bid, and the venture earns a disclosed brokerage fee only if that compliant transfer closes. No price, paid acceptance, buyer commitment, or willingness to pay is evidenced
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A repair, upgrade, insurance event, or repowering job creates removed equipment whose title, functional condition, waste status, and residual value are uncertain

founder_fit: The family installer provides bounded access for testing one workflow without implying a contract or paid demand
Serial-level evidence packs and quote gates fit data-science and automation skills
The no-custody design keeps regulated physical work with authorized and insured counterparties
One class and one region can be time-tracked before any expansion or capital commitment
risks: The installer may reject a separate paid checkpoint or may already receive adequate routing from incumbents.
Incorrect product-versus-waste guidance or incomplete evidence could still create WEEE, shipment, BDO, or liability exposure even without custody.
Partner quotes may be slow, unavailable, or too costly to fit the installer's job schedule.
Commercial string-inverter removals in the pilot area may be too sparse or heterogeneous for repeatable economics.
The workflow and data may remain replicable by installers or established downstream operators.

structure.commercial_archetype: Paid compliance-orchestration workflow with contingent professional brokerage
structure.control_point: A proposed pre-removal route-decision checkpoint embedded in installer work orders, supported by a standardized serial-and-title evidence pack and auditable route record rather than ownership or exclusive supply rights
structure.critical_dependency: Installers must pay for and authorize the checkpoint, while professional buyers and authorized operators must return usable pre-removal quotes quickly enough to select a lawful route; none of those commitments or economics is yet evidenced

thesis: Test a paid, no-custody disposition checkpoint for one equipment-class hypothesis—commercial PV string inverters removed during planned replacement work in one dense region. Before removal, assemble title, serial, condition, and job evidence and obtain both a contingent professional-buyer bid and an authorized-operator route quote. Coordinate direct transfer only when product-status evidence and the bid cover every enumerated landed cost; otherwise route directly to the authorized operator. This replaces dependence on speculative salvage and unsigned first-refusal rights with an unvalidated but directly testable workflow-fee model, while licensed partners retain every regulated physical activity.
title: Pre-Removal Disposition Gate for Commercial PV Inverters
uncertainties: No installer has agreed to embed, authorize, or pay for the pre-removal checkpoint.
No evidence establishes that commercial string inverters are the best pilot class, that removals are dense enough, or that the fixed service fee can exceed fully loaded service cost.
No Polish legal opinion maps the exact classification, advisory-liability, possession, transport, and documentation boundaries of this no-custody workflow.
No authorized operator, tester, insurer, logistics provider, or professional buyer has supplied a binding quote, response-time commitment, or allocation of warranty and return risk.
No paid work-order conversion, repeat usage, acquisition payback, or realized direct-transfer outcome has been observed.
The incidence of stolen, leased, subsidized, warrantied, or otherwise encumbered equipment remains unknown.
